qualification: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618
decision_summary: Curriculum and source traceability are complete, but the present learner experience is not yet uniformly exam-ready. Thirteen lessons have bespoke projections and thirteen rely on a generic DTO fallback; Graph also exceeds the explicit syllabus coding boundary.

complete: 107/107 non-excluded editorial objectives have a current knowledge-unit destination.
55/55 indexed coursebook sections are referenced by the current knowledge units.
58/58 past-paper pattern families occur in lesson authority, marking chains and DTO practice.
29/29 local 2021-2025 Paper 4 mark schemes are represented by current marking-chain samples.
partial: Only 13/26 lessons have a bespoke teacher-approved-for-implementation learner projection; none of those status labels alone is a final release approval.

63/107 assessment requirements are explicitly linked from DTO practice; 44 lack that machine-readable link. Bespoke projections may teach some of them semantically, so this is a traceability gap rather than proof of 44 absent teaching points.
Current marking chains contain representative official atoms and locators, but the practice prompt is often an AlgoCore fixture task rather than a complete past-paper-style worked question.
Nineteen exam-pattern techniques require explicit AlgoCore synthesis because the coursebook supplies only foundations or concepts.
missing: Bespoke student journeys for binary-tree, dictionary, hashing, the four OOP lessons, the four file/exception lessons, graphs and exam-workflow.
A uniform per-lesson question-to-solution-to-marking explanation that preserves the exact QP/MS scenario and states where marks are official versus teacher-created.
A released assessment crosswalk proving every one of the 107 requirements is exercised by a visible learner task.
overreach: The Graph lesson asks learners to implement adjacency-list/matrix Python. Syllabus 2026 p37 explicitly says candidates will not be required to write code for a graph structure.
Recursive binary search is useful transfer practice but is not a separately stated requirement; present it as extension/transfer rather than a core binary-search obligation.
Hashing, performance and graphs are support/corpus-support areas and must not be presented as three equally weighted standalone compulsory coding families.
Random-file bytes/BytesIO is an AlgoCore implementation model; distinguish it from the p40 rule that supplied source files will not contain binary files.

P0: Correct Graph scope immediately: remove coding assessment and retain describe/features/justify-use outcomes.
Produce and teacher-review the 13 missing bespoke learner projections, starting with OOP, file processing/exceptions, binary tree and dictionary.
Close the 44 assessment-requirement traceability gaps or document the exact bespoke task that satisfies each requirement.
For every core lesson, add at least one complete exam-sized worked example: recognise prompt, plan, runnable Python, trace, expected output, error path and QP/MS-grounded mark protection.
P1: Label all 19 coursebook-gap techniques as AlgoCore synthesis from coursebook foundations plus exact QP/MS evidence.
Convert representative marking atoms into plain learner guidance without exposing internal IDs or implying invented Cambridge marks.
Move recursive binary search to an extension/transfer disclosure and add a non-recursive canonical binary-search example first.
Clarify random-file representation, sequential organisation versus sequential access, and the non-binary supplied-file constraint.
P2: Create a teacher-facing matrix showing syllabus objective, book locator, past-paper family, worked example, practice item and release status.
Add timed mixed-paper rehearsal and evidence-document checks only after lesson-level content gates pass.

limitations: This review verifies local source identity, mapping integrity and targeted content semantics; it does not independently re-mark all 672 corpus rows.
A missing DTO assessment-requirement ID does not by itself prove the concept is absent from prose or a bespoke task; it proves the release crosswalk is incomplete.
Coursebook locators support teaching but do not make AlgoCore code or rubrics official Cambridge material.
